text:
Maya Patel: FYI customer (AcmeCorp) opened a ticket — they see p95/p99 regressions on hosted /v1/generate since ~10:30UTC. p95 climbed from ~120ms to ~1.2s, p99 ~2.8s. Impacting interactive flows. /cc @samir @leo :rotating_light:

Samir Rao: thanks Maya. any quick repro or logs? is this single model or all models? sudden deploy?

Maya Patel: repro: curl against our hosted endpoint with tenant header. small payload, just 1 prompt. sample: 
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant: acme" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/trim-7b","input":"Hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
I grabbed metrics from the console: p50 110ms, p95 1.2s, p99 2.8s. Error rate is still low (<0.2%). No deploy events from deploy-bot in the last hour (deploy-bot: nothing).

ops-bot: [alert] High latency detected for route: /v1/generate (tenant=acme) — p95 > 1s for 12m

Leo Chen: pulling runtime metrics now. running `rwdctl metrics query --route /v1/generate --tenant acme --window 15m --percentiles 50,95,99` returns: 
```
{ p50: 0.11, p95: 1.22, p99: 2.81 }
```
Also seeing higher queue depth on the GPU worker pool serving that model: `worker_queue_depth` spiking to 40 vs normal 4.

Samir Rao: that queue depth smells like batching/backpressure. Do we have recent changes to batching config or auto-batch thresholds for this model?

Leo Chen: No config changes in last 24h. But noticed memory pressure on a subset of hosts (gpu-rt-5,6) — OOMs ~ 10:25UTC then recovered. Likely transient but caused requests to pile up and batching to grow. Investigating if kernel selection slowed down on those nodes.

Maya Patel: customer reports it started after they ramped traffic around 10:15UTC (spike x3). They can't throttle. They want an ETA.

Samir Rao: immediate mitigation plan (quick checklist):
1) Apply per-tenant concurrency cap to flatten burst. e.g. set max_concurrency=10 for tenant=acme.
2) Enable per-route circuit breaker to route to fallback model (smaller/quantized) if p95 > 1s for 2 consecutive 5m windows.
3) Force route to another healthy region (us-west-2) as a temporary failover.
4) Reduce batch size and batch timeout for this model to prioritize latency.
5) If needed, scale up worker pool (add 4 more replicas) for the model.

Leo Chen: executing step 1+2 now. running: 
```
rwdctl tenant update --tenant acme --max-concurrency 10
rwdctl route update --route /v1/generate --tenant acme --circuit-breaker true --fallback-model redwood/trim-7b-q4_0 --cb-trigger "p95>1.0s for 2x5m"
```

deploy-bot: deploy started for route-change by leo.eta

Leo Chen: route update completed. also applied batch config tweak: `batch.max_tokens=512`, `batch.timeout_ms=40`, `batch.max_batch=8`.

Samir Rao: good. Also set a temporary tenant rate limit so we don't overload serving cluster while acme ramps: `rlimit.requests_per_minute = 1800` (approx 30r/s).

Kevin Ortiz: I updated the support ticket with a mitigation note and ETA ~15-20m while we watch p95. told them we'll keep fallback model as option if performance doesn't recover.

Maya Patel: customer acked. they asked if we have an SLO guardrail that would have auto-protected them earlier. can we propose something?

Samir Rao: propose these guardrails (short):
- Per-tenant concurrency cap default = 50, configurable per plan. Burst policy: token bucket with 2x baseline for 2m.
- Circuit breaker policy: open when p99 > 1.5s OR p95 > 1.0s for 5m for two consecutive windows. When open, route to fallback smaller model/region and reduce concurrency by 50%.
- Automatic region failover: if region p95 > 1s AND error rate > 0.5% for 5m, route new traffic to secondary region.
- Rate-limit escalation: when p95 rising, dynamically tighten per-tenant RPS by factor until p95 below threshold.

Leo Chen: technical notes for implementation: keep rules in the control-plane as JSON policies. sample policy snippet (applied per-tenant): 
```
{
  "tenant": "acme",
  "circuit_breaker": {
    "p95_threshold_ms": 1000,
    "p99_threshold_ms": 1500,
    "window_minutes": 5,
    "consecutive_windows": 2,
    "fallback_model": "redwood/trim-7b-q4_0",
    "fallback_region": "us-west-2",
    "concurrency_reduction_pct": 50
  }
}
```
(we'll store as string in config service; the control plane will evaluate metrics stream.)

Samir Rao: also want a default auto-scaling guard: if average queue depth > 8 for 3m, add capacity; but cap autoscale to preserve cost.

Maya Patel: after we stabilize, can we run a retro and add an entry to the mitigation playbook? current patch looks good.

Leo Chen: monitoring now. p95 dropped to 280ms after route change + batch tweak + concurrency cap. p99 down to 520ms. queue depth back to normal.

support-bot: ticket updated: "Mitigation applied: per-tenant concurrency cap, fallback model enabled, batch settings reduced. Monitoring p95/p99. Next update in 15m."

Kevin Ortiz: customer replied: thanks, performance improved. asked for a permanent configuration to avoid future regressions. I'll propose the guardrail policy and premium SLA that includes pre-warmed capacity.

Samir Rao: action items:
- Samir: convert these proposed guardrails into a PR for control-plane policies and add unit tests (ETA 2d).
- Leo: add autoscale tweak and safe limits to infra autoscaler (ETA 1d).
- Maya: update mitigation playbook (short runbook steps + commands) and add to internal KB (ETA today).
- Kevin: follow up with customer about SLA / reserved capacity options.

Maya Patel: adding runbook snippet to KB now. quick text for runbook (so the support engineer can copy/paste):
```
1) Run: `rwdctl tenant update --tenant <TENANT> --max-concurrency <N>` (start with 10-20)
2) Run: `rwdctl route update --route <ROUTE> --circuit-breaker true --fallback-model <SMALL_MODEL>`
3) Run: `rwdctl config set --model <MODEL> batch.timeout_ms=40 batch.max_batch=8`
4) If >5m no improvement: `rwdctl scale set --model <MODEL> --replicas +4` or file infra pager
5) Notify customer and schedule follow-up retro
```

Leo Chen: marking thread for follow-up in 24h. Will keep watch for any regression.

Maya Patel: thanks team. :thumbsup:

Samir Rao: noted — please ping again if p95 creeps back up.

ops-bot: [resolved alert] High latency for /v1/generate (tenant=acme) — p95 returned to below threshold

Maya Patel: closing thread once KB is saved.
